newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexicans protest police clampdown on Clinton trip.
newsitem.headline: Mexicans protest police clampdown on Clinton trip.

text.p: Riot police on Tuesday blocked one of Mexico's main political parties from holding an election march, prompting complaints Mexico City was under "a state of seige" during U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit.

About 50 members of the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), whose leader was due to meet Clinton later on Tuesday, scuffled with police who surrounded them and blocked their path, witnesses said.
"They are violating our liberties. It seems they've imposed a state of siege on the capital," Patricia Ruiz, one of the march organisers said.

PRD Congressman Rene Arce complained that the head of the capital's police force, Gen. Enrique Salgado, had ordered a stop to the march to avoid any sign of trouble during Clinton's visit, which ends on Wednesday.
"We accuse Gen. Salgado of obeying the orders of foreign powers, like the United States," he said.
Police have clamped down on security to safeguard Clinton, taking the unusual step of using armed troops at checkpoints. Riot police were sequestered on side streets.

Protests so far have been mostly aimed at recent U.S. moves to toughen its immigration policy, which opponents in Mexico fear will lead to the mass expulsion of Mexicans working illegally in the United States.
The PRD rally was not initially directed against Clinton, its organisers said. It was calling for a more civilised election campaign ahead of Mexico City's July 6 elections.
